text: . The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) hasissued redalert for extremely heavy rainfall over isolated places of Chhattisgarh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana for the next two days. The Met Department has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. The weather department also forecast thunderstorms accompanied with highly gusty winds over Madhya Pradesh and Parts of North-East tomorrow.For Delhi, IMD said the national capital will witness mostly clear skies with no rain. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 34 to 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature of 23 to 25 degrees Celsius.

. President Droupadi Murmu has appointed Governors for six States. Mr. Om Prakash Mathur, who is currently serving as the Governor of Sikkim, will be the new Governor of Keralam. He will replace the current Governor of Keralam, Mr. Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, who has been appointed as the Governor of Tamil Nadu. Mr. Dushyant Gautam has been appointed as the new Governor of Sikkim. Besides, the President has appointed Mr. Braj Mohan Ram as the Governor of Odisha, Dr. Sudha Yadav as the Governor of Karnataka, and Dr. Dhal Singh Bisen as the Governor of Uttarakhand. Their appointments will take effect from the dates on which they assume charge of their respective offices.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today extended greetings on the occasion of the third day of Navratri. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that the day is dedicated to the worship of Goddess Chandraghanta, the symbol of courage, peace, and divine power. He wished everyone happiness, prosperity, and success in their lives.

. Women-led farmer producer organisations are emerging as key drivers of inclusive agricultural growth in India, with nearly 80 per cent of women-led Farmer Producer Companies having more than 600 members. The findings were highlighted in the sixth edition of the State of the FPO Sector 2026 report, launched by the National Association for Farmer Producer Organisations in partnership with NABARD. The report noted that India’s FPO sector has crossed 49,800 registered entities.The report said women-led FPOs have shown stronger survival and resilience after incorporation. They have also recorded improvements in income and market access in several cases. However, low land ownership among women, estimated at around 13 to 14 per cent, and limited access to capital continue to restrict their growth and access to formal finance.To address these challenges, the report recommended formalising the transition from self-help groups to Farmer Producer Companies and ensuring greater participation of women in governance and financial decision-making. NAFPO Steering Committee Chairperson Pravesh Sharma said women should move beyond being beneficiaries of the FPO movement and become its owners, decision-makers and entrepreneurs.

. The Election Commission of India has begun a proactive campaign across the States and Union Territories to ensure that no eligible voter is left out of the voter list. In the national capital, 13 District Election Officers, 70 Electoral Registration Officers, one thousand 313 BLO Supervisors and more than 14 thousand nine hundred Booth Level Officers are working to achieve the objective. The CEO  Delhi has informed that Next Special Camps will be organized at all polling station locations on 18th of October. In various states and union territories special camps are being organised. In Uttar Pradesh Special camps are being held in more than 1 lakh 77 thousand booths. Meanwhile Sikkim has conducted a proactive Special Drive across 623 Polling Stations to ensure no eligible elector is left behind.

. A bipartisan group of US Senators has questioned the legality of President Donald Trump’s decision to allow diesel imports from Russia. The Senators argued that the decision contravened a 2022 law banning such trade until Moscow ends its war in Ukraine. They also said the Trump administration had failed to consult Congress or submit an explanation justifying the decision, as required by law.Following a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday, Trump announced that he had reached a deal with Russia to immediately supply 300,000 tonnes of diesel to the United States and the global market.Trump’s decision came weeks after the US Congress overwhelmingly passed the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which empowers the President to impose sweeping sanctions on Moscow and 100 per cent tariffs on its five largest trading partners in the oil and gas sector.

. In Men’s Cricket, the West Indies defeated India by six wickets in the second T20 International in Ranchi last night, levelling the five-match series to 1-1.Chasing a target of 250 runs, West Indies overhauled the score, posting 252 runs for the loss of four wickets in 18.3 overs, winning the match with nine balls to spare. Captain Shai Hope led from the front with a magnificent 102 off 45 balls, while Sherfane Rutherford’s 84 off 37 set the chase alight.Earlier, put in to bat, India posted a formidable total of 249 for five in stipulated 20 overs. Sanju Samson top-scored for India with a brilliant 82 off 41 balls. Ishan Kishan with 43 off 22 balls also made a valuable contribution. Hope was adjudged Player of the Match for his outstanding performance. The third T20 International between India and West Indies will be played in Indore tomorrow. The match is scheduled to begin at 7 PM.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Andaman and Nicobar Islands, South Interior Karnataka and Uttarakhand tomorrow. It has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds over North Eastern parts of India, including Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura, during the next two days. According to IMD, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada, Odisha and Telangana are also likely to witness similar weather conditions tomorrow.

. India’s Udhayveer Sidhu clinched the gold medal in the men’s 10-metre air pistol event at the International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF), World Cup Rifle and Pistol in Cairo, Egypt, today. The 24-year-old shooter delivered an impressive performance in the medal match, scoring 240.6 points to defeat Germany’s multi-Olympic medallist Christian Reitz by a narrow margin of 0.5 points.Olympic bronze medallists Swapnil Suresh Kusale and Sarabjot Singh are among the leading members of the 24-strong Indian contingent at the tournament, which continues until the 16th of this month. India is competing in eight individual Olympic disciplines and two mixed-team events, with a contingent comprising experienced Olympians and promising young shooters.

. South Korea’s military has said that North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles towards its eastern waters this morning. The launch adds to a recent series of weapons demonstrations that have heightened tensions amid a prolonged freeze in diplomatic engagement.South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said the missiles were fired from an area near the North Korean capital, Pyongyang, where the country has used its airport as a major launch site in recent years.Japan’s Defence Ministry said it had detected at least two missiles and assessed that they had landed in waters outside Japan’s exclusive economic zone. The launch came days after South Korea flight-tested its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon on Friday.While maintaining a hard-line stance towards Seoul, North Korea has stepped up weapons testing as it seeks to expand its arsenal of nuclear-capable systems. These include an October 3 test of what Pyongyang described as a hypersonic intermediate-range missile designed to evade missile defences in South Korea and Japan.The rising tensions have posed a challenge for South Korean President Lee Jae-myung, who favours engagement with North Korea. Lee has also called for strengthening South Korea’s conventional defence capabilities while reducing its reliance on the United States.

. In cricket, India defeated the West Indies by 14 runs in the third T20 International at the Holkar Stadium in Indore last night.Chasing a target of 224 runs, the West Indies managed to score 209 for seven in their stipulated 20 overs. Shimron Hetmyer was the top scorer with 43 runs, while Kamil Pooran scored 42. For India, Arshdeep Singh took three wickets.Earlier, the West Indies won the toss and opted to bowl. Batting first, India were bowled out for 223 in 20 overs. Abhishek Sharma played a superb knock of 69 runs off 30 balls. For the West Indies, Roston Chase, Shamar Joseph and Shamar Springer took two wickets each. Arshdeep Singh was adjudged Player of the Match.India had defeated the West Indies by eight wickets in the opening T20 International in Lucknow. In the second match on Friday, the West Indies beat India by six wickets in Ranchi to level the series. With last night’s victory, India now lead the five-match series 2-1.The fourth match of the series will be played the day after tomorrow at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium in Hyderabad.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand tomorrow. According to IMD, heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh tomorrow. The districts that are likely to receive heavy rainfall include Rampur, Pilibhit, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur and Bahraich. Meanwhile, districts of Madhya Pradesh which are expected to receive rainfall include Satna, Chhatarpur, Tikamgarh and Niwari.IMD said that the line of withdrawal of Southwest Monsoon continues to pass through Gurdaspur, Chandigarh, Muzaffarnagar, Aligarh, Dholpur, Udaipur, Deesa and Naliya.The Met Department has also predicted heavy rainfall over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim for the day. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty windsare expectedto prevail over Punjab, Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe, Telangana, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and parts of Northeast during the next two days.Meanwhile, parts of Delhi are expected to witness light to moderate rainfall tomorrow.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over  Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, Punjab, Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal for tomorrow. Similar weather conditions are expected over Andhra Pradesh and West Rajasthan.  IMD said that conditions are likely to become favourable for further withdrawal of southwest monsoon from some more parts of eastern India and many parts of northeast India during the next two days. Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh and Kerala can also experience thunderstorms accompanied with Lightning.

. India has called for greater access to finance, technology transfer and capacity-building to accelerate the implementation of Sustainable Development Goals, with poverty eradication remaining a key priority.Delivering India’s statement at the UN General Assembly’s Second Committee discussion on Sustainable Development, Counsellor Soumya Nair highlighted the country’s progress in clean energy, noting that non-fossil fuel sources now account for 55 per cent of India’s installed electricity generation capacity. She also highlighted India’s early warning capabilities and its offer to host the Fourth UN World Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction in 2030.Ms Nair underscored India’s commitment to global partnerships through initiatives such as the International Solar Alliance, the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure and the Global Biofuels Alliance. She also reaffirmed India’s support for Small Island Developing States.

. Union Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya today inaugurated the BRICS Traditional and Indigenous Sports Demonstration Games 2026 at the Veer Savarkar Sports Complex in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. The Union Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports organised the games in collaboration with the Gujarat Government.Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Dr. Mandaviya emphasised that traditional and indigenous sports serve as a vital bridge, preserving cultural identity while unlocking new opportunities for global collaboration. The Minister added that under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, initiatives like Khelo India are fostering a sustainable sports ecosystem from the grassroots to the international level.Mentioning upcoming international events in Ahmedabad, Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi proposed five key initiatives for BRICS nations to preserve indigenous sports, including creatinga joint multilingual digital archive and integrating traditional games into academic curricula.Designed as a non-competitive platform, the Games brought together delegations from member and partner countries who presented a diverse range of indigenous sports.

. India’s internet subscriber base has risen to over 111 crore 41 lakh at the end of June this year, from around 109 crore 28 lakh at the end of March 2026, registering a quarterly growth rate of 96%. The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), in its Indian Telecom Services Performance Indicator Report noted that of the total internet subscribers, more than four crore seventy-seven lakh were wired internet subscribers and around one hundred six crore sixty-four lakh were wireless internet subscribers. The Internet subscriber base is comprised of Broadband Internet subscriber base and Narrowband Internet subscriber base. According to the report, the broadband Internet subscriber base increased by 2.03% and the narrowband Internet subscriber base decreased by 0.89% at the end of June 2026. The report also highlighted the growth in India’s telephone subscribers, which increased from around 133 crore at the end of March 2026 to 134 crore at the end of June 2026, registering quarterly growth of 1.31%. India’s overall tele-density also rose from 93.26% at the end of March 2026 to 94.31% at the end of June 2026.

. Bangladesh State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam has said two Bangladeshis have been killed and more than 24 are receiving treatment in hospitals in Riyadh amid the ongoing conflict in Saudi Arabia. Several injured Bangladeshis are in intensive care. Speaking to journalists in Dhaka, she called for an immediate end to the conflict, expressing concern over civilian casualties and the humanitarian situation. According to the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh, ten flights have been affected, disrupting the travel plans of thousands of passengers.

. Saudi Arabia has extended the suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh as authorities continue safety inspections following deadly attacks over the weekend. Saudi Arabia also reported a fresh threat involving drones and cruise missiles on Monday.The General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said the suspension would remain in place while procedures to verify the safety and operational readiness of airport facilities were completed in coordination with the relevant authorities. The extension follows attacks on the airport on October 10 and 11 that killed 14 people and injured hundreds, disrupting air travel and prompting airlines to cancel or suspend services to Saudi Arabia. Several international carriers announced further flight suspensions on Monday, adding to travel disruption across the region.Major General Turki Al-Malki, official spokesman for the Coalition to Support Legitimacy in Yemen, said a threat involving drones and cruise missiles against Saudi Arabia had been detected and tracked and was being dealt with. Earlier in the day, the Coalition had posted that a ballistic missile launched towards Khamis Mushait had been intercepted and destroyed.The Indian Embassy in Riyadh said the family of Mohammed Yousuf Ali, an Indian national who died in the October 10 attack, had decided to hold his funeral in Riyadh. The mission said it was assisting the family with the required formalities. In an update posted on social media, the embassy said three injured Indian nationals remained in intensive care and two more had been admitted to the ICU. Two others were in regular hospital wards, while the remaining injured nationals had been discharged. Embassy officials had visited hospitals treating injured nationals, and the mission said it remained in contact with their families and was providing assistance.The security situation has added urgency to discussions on protecting energy infrastructure and maintaining reliable supplies across the Gulf. Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said on Monday that energy security could not be taken for granted, warning that the current circumstances had tested Saudi Arabia’s infrastructure, institutions and resilience. He made the remarks at the 25th WPC Energy Congress, an international gathering of energy policymakers and industry representatives taking place in Riyadh. The conference has continued despite the airport attacks. The minister also reportedly outlined plans to increase Saudi Arabia’s capacity to export crude oil through pipelines to as much as 10 million barrels per day over the next two to three years.The attacks on the civilian infrastructure have also prompted widespread condemnation and calls for a coordinated regional response. Dr. Anwar Gargash, diplomatic adviser to the UAE president, said the security of Gulf countries was indivisible and described collective security as a shared responsibility.

. The meeting of the Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) examining the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, was held at Parliament Annexe in New Delhi Yesterday. The committee has been tasked with examining the provisions of the Bill and submitting its report to Parliament by the last day of the first week of the Winter Session 2026. Chaired by Lok Sabha BJP MP Sanjay Jaiswal, the Committee heard the views and suggestions of stakeholders, which included representatives from the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India, the Catholic Bishops Conference of India, the All India Christian Council and the Centre for Advancement of Philanthropy. The Committee also interacted with senior Advocate and Rajya Sabha MP Kabil Sibal on the Bill. Later, talking to the media, Mr Sanjay Jaiswal said that the Committee heard the views of everyone presented during the meeting, and subsequently, the JPC  will deliberate these points during its own meeting.The Committee comprises 21 members from the Lok Sabha, nominated by the Speaker, and 10 members from the Rajya Sabha, chaired by Lok Sabha MP Sanjay Jaiswal. The Bill seeks to amend the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, with the objective of making the use of foreign contributions more transparent and accountable.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff.Earlier, India’s three armed services – Army, Navy and the Air Force – planned, trained, procured and advised the government separately. Proposals for greater jointness had been made repeatedly since the Kargil Review Committee of 1999 and the Group of Ministers that followed it, but no single officer held authority across all three services. On the 15th of August 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address, announced the creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff from the ramparts of the Red Fort. Prime Minister Modi said this will lead to better coordination among the three services.The Cabinet approved the decision in December 2019, along with a new Department of Military Affairs within the Ministry of Defence for the CDS to head.  Talking to Akashvani News, retired Lt General Sanjay Kulkarni said the appointment of CDS made it possible for the government to have one point of contact for advice on allmiltarymatters.After the formation of the post of CDS, all three forces have now got effective leadership at the top level.

. Today is World Cotton Day. This day is celebrated annually on October 7 to highlight the global economic, social, and environmental importance of cotton. The theme for this year is Cotton for Good: Building Prosperity Through Trade, Transformation and Partnership. Sharing a video message, Union Textiles Minister Giriraj Singh extended greetings to everyone associated with this sector.He said that this day honours farmers who cultivate cotton in the fields, thereby enabling employment for workers across the entire value chain, whether in spinning mills, ginneries, textile manufacturing units, or garment factories. He informed that 60 lakh farmers in the country are engaged in cotton cultivation. He underlined that countless small enterprises are linked to the handloom industries that not only operate domestically but also export their products.

. Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal has emphasised that the country’s youth must actively participate in India’s development journey by bringing fresh perspectives, innovative ideas, and a strong sense of purpose to policymaking. Addressing the Dilli Dialogue 2026 in New Delhi yesterday, Mr Goyal highlighted India’s resilience and growth trajectory despite global challenges. Mr Goyal stated that India’s market of 1.4 billion people, coupled with its young population, is a significant strength. He pointed out that while several economies are facing ageing populations, India’s average age remains below 30 and is expected to stay so over the next three decades. He further expressed confidence that India’s economy would reach 30 trillion US dollars by 2047.The Minister expressed his confidence in India’s future and the energy and aspirations of youth. He said their ambition and determination make them not merely inheritors of India’s growth story but its architects, driving Bharat towards a future of greater prosperity.

. The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas conducted a special inspection drive in Delhi to assess road dust and effectiveness of road cleaning operations across the city.The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has informed that the commission deployed four flying squad teams for the inspection which was carried out yesterday. The Flying Squad Teams inspected 25 road stretches covering approximately 35 kilometres of the Inner and Outer ring road which come under the jurisdiction of the Public Works Department (PWD), Delhi.The Ministry highlighted that the inspections, which were meant to seek strict implementation of road cleaning and dust mitigation measures, found 17 cases of violation. These violations include accumulation of construction and demolition waste and high visible road dust across inspected road stretches.CAQM has directed PWD, Delhi and other concerned agencies to take appropriate corrective measures to control road dust on priority basis. It also added the inspection shall continue under Operation Clean Air across Delhi-NCR to assess on-ground implementation of various air pollution abatement measures.

. The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.

. Denmark Open Badminton tournament kicks off in Odense today. Two-time Olympic medalist P V Sindhu will take on Olympic champion and world number one An Se-young of South Korea in the Women’s Singles round of 32 match while Tanvi Sharma will be up against Natsuki Nidaira of Japan today. Ashmita Chaliha, Devika Sihag and Unnati Hooda will play their pre quarterfinal matches tomorrow.In Men’s Singles, Lakshya Sen and former world number one Kidambi Srikanth will be in action today in the round of 32 matches, while Ayush Shetty will play tomorrow. In Men’s Doubles, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty will be seen in action tomorrow.

. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has said that under the ongoing 100-week Sankalp Abhiyan, initiatives like MY BHARAT and the National Service Scheme mentored more than 1.06 Lakh participants against substance abuse from across 200 designated institutions and adopted villages.The Ministry highlighted that moving ahead from conventional pledge taking activities, the Yuva Samwad Mela emphasised interactive dialogue, public awareness and cultural expression to encourage informed conversations on the harmful effects of substance abuse.The Ministry, which concluded the first Month of Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan, underscored that the nationwide initiative includes three major components, including youth dialogue, awareness stalls and cultural performances. It also noted that with the completion of its first month, the second month will focus on physical fitness and sports under the theme ‘Fit Youth, Addiction-Free Youth’.

. Russian Presidential Spokesperson Dmitry Peskov today said that the Kremlin has nothing to say on the energy truce issue with Ukraine yet. Peskov also reportedly declined to answer questions about whether the possible energy truce might only apply to oil refineries or other facilities, or with whom specifically contacts are being conducted.Yesterday, US President Donald Trump announced an immediate energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, saying both sides had agreed to stop attacking each other’s energy infrastructure.Trump did not say when the truce was agreed, which facilities it covered, how long it would last, or how it would be monitored.Russia and Ukraine have repeatedly struck each other’s energy infrastructure since the start of conflict in February 2022.

. In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand will be on a two-day visit to India from today. During her visit, she will meet External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar and Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Minister Jayant Chaudhary tomorrow.Meanwhile, Canada’s High Commissioner to India, Christopher Cooter, said that Canada is looking to strengthen bilateral trade with India through a proposed free trade agreement, greater investment and increased movement of people between the two countries. He said tourism between the two countries also offers significant scope for growth.

. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has raised India’s GDP growth forecast to 7 per cent for 2026-27, up from 6.4 per cent in July.  In its flagship World Economic Outlook report, the IMF said the revision in the estimate comes on the back of stronger-than-expected momentum, supported by resilient domestic demand and robust services activity.  It said India stands out with upward revisions, reflecting sustained momentum and growing evidence of stronger growth potential supported by favourable demographic dynamics, an expanding domestic market, and continued structural reforms. The revision came after the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) latest monetary policy meeting, which raised its GDP growth estimate for the current financial year to 7.1 per cent. The IMF has also lifted its FY28 growth projection for India by 0.3 percentage points to 7%, pointing to the durability of the country’s expansion.

. Global crude oil prices reversed course and moved higher today amid skepticism over U.S. President Donald Trump’s announcement of energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia. Brent crude was trading 1.2 per cent up at 105 US dollars and 99 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was also trading over 1.2 per cent higher at 92 US dollars and 98 cents per barrel, at the time of writing this report.

. India have set a target of 224 runs for the West Indies in the third T20 International at Holkar Stadium in Indore. Put into bat, India were all out for 223 runs in the allotted 20 overs. Abhishek Sharma played a superb 69 runs off 30 balls.In reply, West Indies were 16 for 1 in 3 overs, when reports last came in.The five-match series is currently level at one match apiece, after West Indies defeated India by six wickets in the second T20 International in Ranchi on Friday evening. India had defeated West Indies by eight wickets in the opening T20 in Lucknow.

. In Badminton, India’s Anmol Kharb has won the Women’s Singles title at the Türkiye International Challenge. She defeated her compatriot Aakarshi Kashyap in straight games, 21-11, 21-14 in the final. This marks Anmol’s third international senior title. Meanwhile, India’s Suraj Goala and Nicholas Raj finished runners-up at the Men’s Doubles event. The Indian pair lost to Denmark’s William Kryger Boe and Rasmus Espersen in the final, 14-21, 19-21.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has called for doubling India-UK Bilateral trade by 2030. Mr Goyal said this while addressing the JETCO Business Plenary under the 16th Session of the India-UK Joint Economic and Trade Committee (JETCO) in New Delhi today. Mr Goyal reaffirmed India’s commitment to deepening India-UK economic cooperation through sustained engagement, stronger institutional mechanisms, and enhanced collaboration. He said, this will unlock new opportunities for businesses in both countries.The Minister called upon businesses in India and the United Kingdom to translate the opportunities created by the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) into expanded trade, investment, partnerships and job creation. Mr Goyal said CETA marks a major milestone in the economic partnership between the two countries, providing zero-duty access in the United Kingdom market for most Indian exports while opening up significant opportunities for UK exporters across sectors. He said the wide-ranging CETA had opened up numerous opportunities to expand trade, encourage new exporters and introduce new product lines.Highlighting the existing trade complementarities, Mr Goyal noted that India was a major exporter of smartphones, pharmaceutical products, jewellery, textiles, leather goods, rice and certain agricultural products, iron and non-alloy steel, machinery parts and auto components. On the UK side, he identified potential in the supply of products across the petroleum value chain, technology products in electronics and electrical equipment, medicaments and motor cars.

. Mongolian President Ukhnaagiin Khurelsukh today visited the Oil Refinery Construction site at Altanshiree Soum in Mongolia’s Dornogobi Province and thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi for India’s unwavering support for the strategically important project.According to the India Embassy in Ulaanbaatar, Khurelsukh expressed satisfaction with the progress of the strategically important project, which is expected to enable Mongolia to produce its own refined fuel.During the visit, he also interacted with the engineers and workers involved in the construction and appreciated Indian Ambassador to Mongolia Atul Malhari Gotsurve’s role in advancing the project.During Prime Minister Modi’s visit to Mongolia in 2015, a Line of Credit (LOC) of one billion US dollar was approved for development of infrastructure, which the Government of Mongolia decided to utilise for construction of its first-ever oil refinery in Dornogobi Province with a capacity of 1.5 million metric tonnes per annum (MMTPA).

. Principal Secretary to Prime Minister P.K. Mishra today said data collection and analysis are essential for evidence-based policymaking, particularly in the era of artificial intelligence. Addressing the  Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation Conclave at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, Mr Mishra said data would form the foundation of India’s development journey. He called for closer coordination between the Centre and states to harmonize data collection, adopt common definitions and use standard classifications. Mr Mishra said data generated at the state and district levels will play a crucial role in compiling national statistics, including estimates of gross domestic product. He added India had undergone major transformation over the past decade, with significant progress in infrastructure, digital public services, financial inclusion and entrepreneurship. He underscored that Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047 must be measurable, with reliable data helping assess the country’s progress toward becoming a prosperous, inclusive, innovative and sustainable nation.

. Most Asian stock indices displayed mixed trends today. South Korea’s Kospi index plunged over 3.6 per cent, China’s Shanghai Composite Index fell more than 0.4 per cent, and Taiwan’s Taiex index dipped marginally. Conversely, Singapore’s Strait Times index as well as Hong Kong’s Hang Seng declined a quarter of a per cent. Meanwhile, Japan’s market remained closed on account of a holiday.In European markets, Germany’s DAX gained 0.8 per cent, while London’s FTSE 100 also added nearly 0.8 per cent, when reports last came in.

. The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has said that 139 people, including 15 children, have died after an overcrowded boat carrying 305 migrants capsized near Guhere, north of Obock, off the coast of Djibouti in East Africa. The IOM reported that the vessel sank close to the shore shortly after departing on Thursday night.The official death toll stands at 139. However, IOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti, Alexandre Coissac, clarified that the figure includes only those whose bodies were buried by local authorities, while other victims were buried directly by migrants. 84 people remain missing as search-and-rescue operations continue, and the agency has warned that the death toll could rise.More than 80 survivors, all Ethiopian nationals, were rescued. Local authorities moved them to the IOM Rescue Centre in Obock, where they are receiving psychological support and medical care.The boat was travelling across the Bab el-Mandeb Strait from Djibouti to Yemen. This route is part of a popular but highly dangerous migration corridor used by tens of thousands of people from the Horn of Africa seeking work and safety in Gulf countries. According to the IOM’s Missing Migrants Project, more than 900 migrants died or went missing along this route last year alone.

. India is hosting the first Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation, BIMSTEC Home Ministers’ Meeting in New Delhi. This historic meeting highlights the collective commitment to combating terrorism, transnational organized crime, narcotics, radicalization, human trafficking, illicit financial flows, and cyber threats.Speaking on the occasion, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said that BIMSTEC has emerged as an important platform for regional integration, economic cooperation and collective security. He said India has always been committed to peace and human welfare, guided by the principle of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam. Mr Shah reiterated that India respects the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries and believes in the peaceful resolution of disputes.Reaffirming India’s policy of zero tolerance towards terrorism, the Union Home Minister called for a collective commitment to ensure that no terrorist network finds space within the region for shelter, recruitment, training, financing or activities against neighbouring countries. Mr Shah also emphasised mutual assistance in extradition and legal cooperation, in accordance with national laws and applicable treaties. He said criminal networks operate across borders and exploit local vulnerabilities. Mr Shah stressed the need for real-time cooperation and coordination among intelligence, law enforcement, financial monitoring and border management agencies.On counter-terrorism cooperation, the Minister stressed the exchange of actionable intelligence through designated nodal agencies and better coordination against terrorist financing and organised crime. Mr Shah said India has achieved significant success in bringing fugitive criminals back from different parts of the world to face justice. He appealed to all BIMSTEC members to strengthen cooperation to ensure that no criminal or terrorist can evade the law, regardless of where they are hiding.BIMSTEC is a regional organisation established in 1997 to promote economic and technical cooperation among countries around the Bay of Bengal and its neighbourhood. It has seven member states: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. It aims to promote economic and technical cooperation among countries bordering the Bay of Bengal and in its neighbourhood.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the Centre has embodied the principle of Power to Empower in its governance approach and work culture. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Mr Modi said that India’s progress is rooted in collective growth and shared opportunities. He said that power is not just the ability to move ahead, but it is also the ability to empower others. He said that in the present era, digital power has emerged as one of the key drivers of this transformation and is playing a significant role in advancing this vision. Mr Modi stated that digital power has opened up greater opportunities for India.Prime Minister Modi said that India’s economic growth is taking place on a strong foundation amidst global uncertainty. He said the GDP growth stood at 7.8% in the first quarter of this financial year. Mr Modi highlighted that today, India’s foreign exchange reserves exceed 700 billion dollars and the banking system is in its strongest position in many decades. Prime Minister said India’s reform express continues to move ahead at high speed.Prime Minister said that India’s progress in the twenty-first century is a story of advancing together with everyone and carrying everyone along. He said, whenever the world needs a steady pillar, India extends its hand in support, recognizing its responsibility. Mr Modi said today, India is home to more than two thousand Global Capability Centres that are providing services to companies across the world.Prime Minister said technology, data, knowledge and innovation have become important sources of power in the twenty-first century. He said, the government constant endeavour is to ensure that India’s capabilities open new doors of opportunity for other countries as well. Mr Modi said, India is the Mother of Democracy, and it has over 100 languages, around 80,000 registered newspapers and publications, and more than one thousand satellite television channels.’ Mr Modi highlighted that India had lifted twenty-five crore people out of poverty over the past decade.Prime Minister Modi said India’s startup ecosystem has expanded significantly since 2014, with the number of startups crossing 2,50,000. He noted that nearly half of these startups come from smaller cities and towns, while more than 45% have at least one woman director or partner.

. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today felicitated sportspersons from the three Services for winning 27 medals at the recently concluded Asian Games in Japan. The athletes won six gold, eleven silver and ten bronze medals, contributing significantly to India’s overall tally of 85 medals andfourth-place finish. Addressing the athletes, Mr Singh praised their discipline, hard work and team spirit. He lauded the Mission Olympic Wing, coaches and support staff for their role in identifying and nurturing sporting talent.Defence Minister reiterated the Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led Government’s commitment to strengthening India’s sporting ecosystem, with sustained focus on infrastructure, modern training facilities and better opportunities for athletes.The Defence Minister also urged the athletes and trainers to adopt a focused approach towards the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, expressing confidence that the Services would deliver an even stronger performance.

In Pakistan, police have taken former Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi and seven other Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) leaders into protective custody following the imposition of emergency rule amid deteriorating security. The detentions come as the party stages protests demanding the release of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan and access to medical treatment for him.Those detained include Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati and PTI provincial president Junaid Akbar. Police also arrested 56 PTI workers in Swabi.President Asif Ali Zardari imposed emergency rule on Sunday, citing a rise in terrorist attacks and a breakdown of the constitutional machinery. The provincial bureaucracy has been reshuffled, while an advisory council will assist the governor in administering the province.Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Peshawar on Monday to chair a high-level security meeting. The PTI rejected allegations of links with militants and accused the federal government of failing to provide adequate counterterrorism resources.The party’s demands include access to Khan’s personal doctors, the release of detained supporters and his sisters, and medical care for his wife, Bushra Bibi. Khan has been in prison since 2023.

. The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics has been awarded to American economists Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford for developing macroeconomic models that help policymakers stabilise economies during booms and recessions. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences said their work has strengthened the theoretical basis for fiscal and monetary policies and improved governments’ and central banks’ ability to respond to economic fluctuations.The Nobel Committee said, the economists developed models based on how households and businesses make decisions about spending, saving, investment and pricing, taking future economic conditions into account. Their research has helped policymakers understand how government policies and central bank signals influence economic activity. The models are now widely used by central banks and governments around the world.Robert E. Hall is a professor at Stanford University, while Michael Woodford is a professor at Columbia University. The prize carries an award of 12 million Swedish kronor, which will be shared equally between the two laureates.

. In Nepal, more than 100 foreign trekkers are stranded at various locations after flooding over the weekend swept away hiking trails and bridges in the country’s central region. Authorities rescued 321 people, including 12 foreigners, today after a pre-dawn landslide in Gorkha district, about 100 kilometres west of Kathmandu, blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, triggering downstream flooding. The army said rescue operations would continue tomorrow, even as the river’s water level receded. The Budhi Gandaki is a tributary of the Trishuli River, which was affected by a catastrophic flood in August following a glacier collapse in another tributary. The disaster killed 1,457 people, while thousands remain missing. No fatalities were reported in the latest flooding.

The Government has the draft National Steel Policy-Vision 2047, which provides a long-term policy framework to build a globally competitive, technologically advanced, environmentally sustainable and resource-efficient steel sector. The Policy aims to meet the country’s growing steel requirements while strengthening India’s position in the global steel industry. The policy projects the country’s per capita steel consumption rising to 302 kilograms from the current 116 kilograms, while India’s crude steel production has already increased from 89 million tonnes in 2014-15 to 170 million tonnes in 2025-26. The Policy also projects an increase in the country’s steel exports to 45 MT by 2047. Further, it says that India aims for a near threefold expansion in crude steel-making capacity to 604 million tonnes by 2047 and to raise finished steel demand to 505 million tonnes.The draft Policy focuses on promoting greater use of steel in infrastructure, housing, transportation, renewable energy, and emerging manufacturing sectors. It also places emphasis on cleaner steel production, seeking to lower average emissions intensity from 2.54 tonnes of carbon dioxide per tonne of crude steel to 1.54 tonnes by 2047 through measures including greater energy efficiency, renewable electricity, increased scrap use and hydrogen-based steel-making.

. India has called for terrorist acts that meet the threshold of crimes against humanity to be covered under the proposed international convention on the prevention and punishment of such crimes. Speaking at the UN General Assembly’s Sixth Committee, Counsellor at India’s UN Mission, R. Mythili, said the issue should be addressed in line with the framework of the proposed convention. She stressed that nations must retain primary responsibility for protecting people, ensuring accountability for grave violations and exercising jurisdiction, while respecting the rights of the accused and the interests of victims. Ms. Mythili also underlined that measures to prevent and punish crimes against humanity must respect national sovereignty and the principle of non-interference in internal affairs. The convention is expected to be adopted at an international conference in 2028.

. India’s Putul Sonowal has created history by assuring the country’s first-ever medal at the World Bowls Champion of Champions in Barham, Australia. The 43-year-old from Assam achieved the milestone by reaching the semi-finals of the men’s singles event. Sonowal defeated Singapore’s Harriman Yuen in the quarter-finals to secure his place in the last four.A member of the Assam Police, Sonowal has emerged as one of India’s leading lawn bowls players. He won the Men’s Singles gold medal at the 2026 Asian Lawn Bowls Championship, further strengthening his standing on the international stage. Earlier, at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Sonowal defeated Canada’s Ryan Bester, a three-time Commonwealth Games medallist and former world outdoor champion, in the Men’s Singles event. The match went to a tie-break after both players won one set each, with Sonowal emerging victorious.
